Confirmed: `init()` creates the `TickCounter` and never calls `reset()` on it before the first `update()` call, yet the constructor (as introduced in 65a7383) sets `tickCount = maxTicks`. This means the very first `update()` call after game init would immediately report the round as finished (0 ticks processed), i.e., every game session's first round would end instantly.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 65a7383f98f831cf957630ed5750bf2ec7f249cf

## Reasoning
(1) The fix commit (16840bb) touches `TickCounter.java`, removing the line `tickCount = maxTicks;` from the constructor and updating the constructor's javadoc (removing "Has to be reset() first to get used"). Since this was the only substantive logic change in `TickCounter.java` in the fix diff (the rest of the commit is an unrelated large refactor for round-end/mid-round-loading), I traced the file's history with `git log` and found `TickCounter.java` was newly introduced in commit 65a7383 ("Cleans up and simplifies the game's processing in the session").

(2) In 65a7383, the `TickCounter` constructor set `tickCount = maxTicks;` at the end — meaning a freshly constructed counter already reports itself as "finished" (`tickCount == maxTicks`). The class's own javadoc even warned "Has to be reset() first to get used," but I checked `GameSession.init()` (introduced/modified in the same commit) and confirmed it constructs the `TickCounter` and never calls `reset()` on it before the first `update()` invocation. `reset()` is only called later, inside `startNextRound()`.

(3) Consequence: on the very first `update()` call after a game session is initialized, `TickCounter.update()` immediately sees `tickCount == maxTicks` and returns `true`, signaling that the round is already over — before a single tick/fixedUpdate has run. This is exactly the kind of bug the fix addresses by removing the premature `tickCount = maxTicks` assignment so a new counter starts at 0 and requires actual elapsed ticks before signaling round-end.

I'm reasonably confident in this identification since the removed line directly corresponds to the described logic bug and the call site never performed the documented workaround (`reset()`), but I did not find an explicit issue/test confirming the exact observed symptom, so some residual uncertainty remains.
